sentence: This project teaches scientists about the genetics and genomics of human disease, using medical genetics, mouse genetics and model systems.
This project builds research skills in scientists to help control vector-borne diseases, including malaria and arboviral diseases.
This project tests whether existing technologies for designing proteins that travel to specific parts of a cell can improve T cell responses.
This project studies which cells and genes in human joints and nerves are linked to current and long-term chronic neck pain.
This project offers cancer genomics services, including next-generation sequencing, microarray technologies and computational data analysis, for genomics experiments.
This project develops deep learning methods to find Alzheimer's disease features in neuroimaging data and link them to genetic data.
This project studies the short- and long-term immune responses to the COVID-19 mRNA vaccine in adolescents, children and mother-infant pairs.
This project studies molecular factors that promote inflammation and gastric cancer after chronic infection, and their role in resistance to chemotherapy.
This project tests senolytic drugs in human lung and ovary tissue models and develops blood-based biomarkers that monitor how well they work.
This project studies how membrane contact sites between organelles shape the response of macrophages to fungal infection.
This project builds computational tools to find out how regulators after transcription and genetic variants shape protein abundance and function.
This project studies how modifications of Dicer and small RNA pathways control germ cell development and the oocyte-to-embryo transition.
This project builds early warning tools that use vital sign analysis to detect sepsis and necrotizing enterocolitis in premature infants.
This project develops a nanomedicine that targets tumors and works with immune checkpoint blockade to treat metastatic colorectal cancer.
This project prepares cancer biologists to work well in the changing field of cancer biology.
This project explores how to adapt an intervention that supports caregivers of older adults with dementia who are at high risk.
This project studies at atomic detail how chloride channels, transporters and scramblases work and how disease-causing mutations impair them.
This project uses ecological momentary assessment and co-design with young adults to build a mobile intervention for managing chronic pain.
This project measures the size, concentration and protein content of lipoprotein particles using ion mobility analysis and mass spectrometry.
This project studies how DNA polymerases and other proteins repair double strand breaks in DNA, especially damaged breaks.
